taxonomy:
Here’s a practical taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, organized by the main solving mechanic.

## 1) Shading / Coloring puzzles
These ask you to paint cells black/gray or leave them white, usually under local shape or count constraints.

- **Akari** — place bulbs; light coverage puzzle
- **Hitori** — black out duplicates while keeping white cells connected
- **Heyawake** — shade cells with room-count and connectivity rules
- **Kurodoko** — shade black cells so numbered cells see a specified count of whites
- **Nurikabe** — build a connected black wall around numbered white islands
- **Usowan** — shade cells so one clue per region is wrong
- **Nurimeizu** — paint walls to create a maze from S to G
- **Nurimisaki** — shade non-promontory cells; white cells form promontories
- **Norinori** — place black domino-like pairs in regions
- **LITS** — shade tetrominoes in regions, with adjacency constraints
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles to leave rectangles/squares of white
- **Sto-stone** — shade cells so “dropped” stones satisfy room counts
- **Choco Banana** — divide into white/gray matching shapes and counts
- **Double Choco** — partition into blocks containing matching white/gray areas
- **Nuritwin** — shade regions into exactly two same-sized blocks
- **Tilepaint** — shade tiles to reveal an outline
- **Five Cells** — partition into 5-cell blocks with line-count clues
- **Chained Block** — fill black-cell blocks into chains with shape uniqueness
- **Evolomino** — block growth/shape progression puzzle
- **Sashigane** — form L-shaped blocks with bend/end clues
- **Shikaku** — divide into rectangles with one number each
- **Fillomino** — partition into same-number regions sized by their number

## 2) Loop / Path puzzles
These require drawing one continuous loop or a set of non-branching paths.

- **Slitherlink** — single loop around dot clues
- **Masyu** — loop with black/white pearl turn/straight rules
- **Masyu** — single loop with pearl constraints
- **Yajilin** — loop plus black-cell placement from arrow clues
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop through white circles with turn/straight area rules
- **Mid-loop** — loop through black circles as midpoints of segments
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop visits rooms in alternating moon/sun pattern
- **Suraromu** — loop passes through gates in order from a start circle
- **Nagareru** — loop follows arrow-defined wind direction constraints
- **Numberlink** — connect matching numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hebi** — snake-number paths with directional visibility constraints
- **Pencils** — draw pencil lines from tips using length clues
- **Satogaeri** — move circles through tracks to countries
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

## 3) Number-placement / Latin-style puzzles
These are primarily about filling numbers according to region or row/column rules.

- **Sudoku** — classic row/column/box 1–9 placement
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers and arrow maxima
- **Ripple Effect** — room-based consecutive numbering with spacing rules
- **Nansuke** — place numbers from a given list into blanks
- **Juosan** — fill with horizontal/vertical marks under region totals
- **Kurotto** — black-cell counts around circles
- **Hashiwokakero** — bridge-count puzzle, number clues on islands
- **Fillomino** — number regions by size
- **Shikaku** — rectangle partition with area numbers

## 4) Connection / Graph / Bridge puzzles
These focus on linking objects under degree, continuity, or pairing constraints.

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect islands with bridges
- **Numberlink** — pair matching numbers with paths
- **Yajilin** — loop plus directional black-cell counting
- **Satogaeri** — route circles through tracks to countries
- **Nuritwin** — connected shaded components across regions
- **Chained Block** — blocks must form chains by corner contact

## 5) Shape / Polyomino / Tiling puzzles
These emphasize packing or identifying shapes.

- **LITS** — tetromino placement
- **Evolomino** — shape evolution/growth
- **Choco Banana** — paired same-shape areas in blocks
- **Double Choco** — same-shape white/gray area pairing
- **Shakashaka** — triangle tiling to leave rectangular white spaces
- **Sashigane** — L-shaped block decomposition
- **Nuritwin** — two equal blocks per region
- **Shikaku** — rectangle tiling
- **Five Cells** — 5-cell blocks

## 6) Visibility / Line-of-sight / Counting puzzles
These use “see until blocked” rules, directional counts, or ray-like effects.

- **Akari** — illumination in rows/columns
- **Kurodoko** — number sees to nearest black cell/frame
- **Hebi** — directional snake visibility
- **Kurotto** — sum of contiguous black cells around circles
- **Makaro** — arrow points to max adjacent number
- **Pencils** — line length from tip
- **Ripple Effect** — spacing between repeated numbers
- **Yosenabe** — circles move into target areas, avoiding crossings
- **Nagareru** — wind direction affects loop movement
- **Suraromu** — gate-order traversal from a start
- **Nurimisaki** — promontory straight-line white counts

## 7) Hybrid constraint puzzles
These combine multiple mechanism types.

- **Heyawake** — shading + room counts + connectivity + anti-rectangle
- **Nurikabe** — shading + island counts + connectivity + no 2×2 black
- **Yajilin** — loop + shading
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop + room alternation
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop + area-based turn/straight behavior
- **Makaro** — numbers + arrows + room uniqueness
- **Nurimeizu** — maze + shading + global path constraints
- **Satogaeri** — movement + routing + region assignment

---

# A more structural taxonomy

If you want a more “design-oriented” taxonomy, these games can also be grouped by what they operate on:

## A. Cell-state puzzles
Change cell colors/states.
- Akari, Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Norinori, Nurikabe, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Usowan, Tilepaint, Choco Banana, Double Choco, Nuritwin, Sashigane, Shikaku, Fillomino, Five Cells

## B. Path-drawing puzzles
Draw one loop or many paths.
- Slitherlink, Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Nagareru, Numberlink, Yajilin, Pencils, Hebi

## C. Number-placement puzzles
Fill numbers or use number clues heavily.
- Sudoku, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Nansuke, Kurotto, Juosan, Fillomino, Shikaku, Hashiwokakero

## D. Motion / transformation puzzles
Move items rather than just assign cells.
- Satogaeri, Yosenabe

## E. Shape-partition puzzles
Partition into geometric pieces.
- Shikaku, Sashigane, LITS, Five Cells, Evolomino, Choco Banana, Double Choco, Nuritwin, Shakashaka
